proof.criterion: The refactor of this round: askPartLinks, one fragment the issue closure and the document's own incoming read share, keeps both consumers and the ask's own refs row (review findings 3 and 9).
proof.surface: The same running Dispatch, over HTTP and through dispatch read --issue.
proof.command: GET /api/v1/artifacts/<document>/references, GET /api/v1/references?to=<document> and dispatch read --issue <the asking issue>, for a document cited from an option alone, then from a person's answer alone, then from a question alone, then from a question and an option together
proof.observed: Option alone: the document read answers referenced_by [{"kind":"ask","id":"ede7acdf-…","excerpt":"The question names nothing."}], the closure prints "CORE/r3doc-… · depth 1 via ask ede7acdf-…", and the graph read lists mentions ask/ede7acdf-…#b2. Answer alone: both the document read and the closure list the ask. Question alone: the document read still lists the ask, so the ask-level arm survived the refactor. Question and an option together: the ask is listed once, and two asks citing the same document are listed once each.
proof.negativeControl: Dropping the one citing option empties all three together — referenced_by [], the closure "- none", the graph read [] — so each read follows the live part rather than a row left behind.

proof.criterion: The refactor of this round: AskPartIDs, the one owner of the matching of stored parts to an ask's options and answer (review finding 10), still answers by identity and not by position.
proof.surface: The same running Dispatch, over HTTP, with the ask row moved under the index by a direct SQL update — what a stale index or an older build leaves.
proof.command: update asks set options = … directly in PostgreSQL, then GET /api/v1/asks/<id>; and an ask whose two options render to the same part text
proof.observed: Two options swapped under the index keep their own ids (Beta b3, Alpha b2), so an id follows the text; a row grown by one gives the new option id null; a shrunk row keeps the survivor's b3. Two options whose rendered text is identical have equal text_sha256 in ask_blocks (c824ca3cbe for both) and still take b2 and b3, each reference reading its own part.
proof.negativeControl: The swap is the control: a matcher that fell back to position would answer Beta b2 and Alpha b3, the defect the second review found, and it answers Beta b3 and Alpha b2.

proof.criterion: Review finding 3 of this round (important): the five published texts give the reply rule the code keeps.

proof.observed: The served description reads "A reply names the comment it answers in reply_to, and one block of it in reply_to_block; with ask_id in place of reply_to, reply_to_block names one part of that ask." CreateCommentInput.reply_to_block says the block is "a block of the comment reply_to names, checked against that comment before reply_to climbs to its thread's head, in an ask's thread as anywhere else, or, with ask_id, a part of that ask"; Comment.reply_block says the same; AGENTS.md's route row and the changelog fragment carry the same rule.
